KEY MESSAGE 1...
Severe Thunderstorm Watch #687 has been issued for Ulster, 
Dutchess and Litchfield Counties until 10 pm EDT. The greatest 
threat for any severe thunderstorms is from a line or broken 
line of t-storms that could produce wind gusts 58 mph or 
greater which could break large tree limbs, down some trees, 
power poles and lines. The latest SPC RAP Mesoanalysis shows 
very little SB CAPE on the order of 100 J/kg in the watch area. 
Some of the CAMS show small amounts of instability 100-250 J/kg 
with increasing 0-6 km Bulk Shear 50-65 KT. The greatest threat 
window looks like 5-730 pm. The forecast was updated to include 
the wording some may be severe for these 3 counties. Some gusty 
showers or an isolated thunderstorms (winds 35-50 mph) may occur
north of the watch area.

Previous...A strong cold front continues to approach from west-
central NY and PA this afternoon, as low pressure moves towards
southern Quebec. A strong positively-tilted trough mid and 
upper level associated with the system is moving across the 
eastern Great Lakes Region and the Midwest. Pre- frontal showers
continue across the southern Adirondacks and w-central Mohawk 
Valley. Some breaks in the clouds occurred across the Capital 
District/Schoharie Valley earlier but stratus has increased 
again across most of the region. A high shear-low CAPE 
environment is setting up from the Mohawk Valley/Capital 
Region/Berkshires south and east. SPC has most of the forecast 
area in Marginal (Level 1 of 5) or Slight Risk (Level 2 of 5) 
due to some low-topped convection potentially forming that may 
bring some isolated damaging wind gusts to the southern portion 
of the forecast area. 

The latest HREFS/REFS has limited mean SBCAPEs of 100-250 J/kg 
south of the Capital District over the mid Hudson Valley, 
southeast Catskills, southern Taconics, and NW CT. The 0-6 km 
bulk shear increases 40-60+ KT. The CAMs soundings from the 3-km
HRRR/ARW-WRF show 800 hPA winds increasing to 45-50 KT with the
low to mid level winds very strong. A broken line or strongly- 
forced line of convection is possible on some of the CAMs with 
the threat looking the greatest from about Hudson, NY to the 
I-84 corridor. The question will be if any updrafts will be tall
enough to tap into these winds aloft and translate them to the 
sfc. At the very least, we could be looking at some gusty 
showers with a rumble of thunder with gusts 30-50 mph which 
could blow around loosely unsecured objects, and bring down 
some foliated large tree limbs. The the threat window looks like
3-7 pm before the showers and possibly some embedded
strong/potentially severe thunderstorms move east of most of 
the forecast area with the front. 

KEY MESSAGE 2...

Tonight, in the wake of the cold front brisk/blustery 
conditions occur, as west/northwest winds 10-20 mph shift to the
northwest with the cold advection. Some gusts 25-35 mph will 
likely occur with a few isolated gusts around 40 mph funneling 
down the Mohawk Valley into the Capital Region, northern 
Taconics and the Berkshires. Some gusty winds are also possible 
over the northern/eastern Catskills. In the wake of the front 
with the mid and upper trough approaching, some upslope rain to
snow showers will occur over the western Dacks and southern 
Greens. Some light snow accums of a coating to a few tenths of 
inch may occur. Some light snow showers/flurries could occur 
over the northern Catskills, northern Taconics and Berkshires 
due to upslope and lake enhanced showers. The low-level flow 
quickly veers to the northwest with some multi-bands of lake 
effect potentially grazing the northern and eastern Catskills 
Saturday morning. Latest NAEFS indicate H850 temp anomalies 
will be 1 to 2 STDEVs below normal. The actual H850 temps fall 
to -6C to -9C from Albany north and west into the Adirondacks 
to 0C to -6C readings south and east towards the I-84 corridor 
by daybreak Saturday. Temps will fall quickly with widespread 
lows in the 30s to lower 40s with some upper 20s over the 
south/southwest Adirondacks and southern Greens. Wind chill 
temps or "feels-like" temps when combining the winds with the 
air temps will be in the teens to mid/upper 20s over the higher
terrain with mainly 30s in the valleys with some mid/upper 20s 
in the western Mohawk Valley. It will feel like early Winter. 

Upslope and lake effect snow showers/flurries or sprinkles will end 
in the late morning with the subsidence inversion lowering. The
brisk northwest winds will continue with chilly temps with 
daytime highs only in the 40s in the valleys with a few readings
near 50F in the Hudson Valley and 30s to lower 40s over the 
hills and mtns. The winds will persist from the northwest at 
10-20 mph with some gusts 25-35 mph due to the sfc pressure 
gradient and some deeper mixing. We increased gusts slightly
